subject: ancient-history
topicName: Pericles & the Golden Age of Athens

questions.question: Q: How did Pericles maintain his political influence for so long?

points.text: Pericles was repeatedly elected strategos (general), one of the few offices that could be held multiple times. He used his authority and oratory to persuade the assembly, introduced state pay for office-holders (attracting popular support), and used Delian League tribute to fund public building that provided jobs and beautified Athens.

questions.question: Q: Why was the building programme controversial?

points.text: Pericles used Delian League tribute (intended for defence against Persia) to fund magnificent buildings on the Acropolis, including the Parthenon. Allies resented their money being spent on Athenian glorification rather than collective security. Plutarch records that opponents accused Pericles of adorning Athens like a vain woman with jewels bought with other people's money.

questions.question: Q: What did Pericles' Funeral Oration celebrate?

points.text: In 431 BC, Pericles honoured fallen soldiers by celebrating Athens itself: its democracy (power in the hands of the many), freedom, openness, cultural achievements and the willingness of citizens to die for their city. Thucydides presents it as an idealised vision of Athenian values.

questions.question: Q: What caused the Peloponnesian War?

points.text: Growing tension between Athens' expanding empire and Sparta's fear of Athenian power. Athens' imperialism threatened Spartan allies, and trade disputes with Corinth (Sparta's ally) escalated. The immediate cause was Athenian interference in a Corinthian colony (Corcyra) and the Megarian decree restricting trade. Sparta declared war to 'free the Greeks' from Athenian tyranny.

questions.question: Q: How did the plague affect Athens?

points.text: The plague struck Athens in 430 BC when the rural population was crowded within the city walls. It killed about a third of the population, caused social breakdown (lawlessness, despair) and undermined Pericles' strategy. Pericles himself died of the plague in 429 BC.
